p4.title: My bedroom
p4.text: My bedroom is small but I love it. My __(0)__ is next to the window. On the wall there is a big picture of a __(1)__. I have got a lot of __(2)__ in a box under the bed. My favourite one is a green robot. At night, I read a __(3)__ in bed. My cat sleeps on my __(4)__. In the morning, my mum says 'Get up!' and I __(5)__ my room.

parts.text: Kim has got a small brown dog. His name is Bobby. Today Kim can't find Bobby. He is not in the garden and he is not in the kitchen.

items.q: Where is Bobby not? Not in the garden and not in the …

parts.text: Kim looks under the bed and behind the sofa. Then she hears a noise in the bathroom. Bobby is in the bath with a big yellow duck!

items.q: Where does Kim hear a noise?
What is in the bath with Bobby?

parts.text: Kim laughs. Bobby is wet! Kim washes Bobby with soap and water. Now Bobby is clean and he sleeps on his bed.

items.q: Where does Bobby sleep at the end?

questions.q: How many people are there in your family?

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
This is my house. Look at the girl on the sofa. She's got a cat.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
That's Bill. He watches TV every afternoon.
Look at the kitchen. Can you see the girl drinking milk at the table?
Yes, it is. Jill drinks milk every day.
And who's the boy on the floor? He's got a robot.
That's Dan. It's his new robot.
Can you see the girl by the window? She's got a doll.
Who's the boy next to the door with the big blue ball?
That's Hugo. He wants to play in the garden.
Hugo. His ball is very big!
p2: Part Two. Listen and write a name or a number. There are two examples.
And how old are you, Kim?
Can you see the answers? Now you listen and write a name or a number.
And what's the number of your house?
Yes. I've got a dog. His name's Bobby.
Bobby? How do you spell that?
Is your new house big? How many bedrooms are there?
There are three bedrooms. One is for me!
p3: Part Three. Look at the pictures. Listen and tick the box. There is one example.
Mum, where's the cat? Is it under the table?
No, it's on your bed. Look! It's sleeping.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
No, Sam. I'm cooking pizza today. Your favourite!
Two. What is in the box?
Dad, what's in this box? Is it a kite?
No. Open it and look. It's a robot!
Three. Which room is Dad cleaning?
Dad, are you cleaning the kitchen?
No. I'm cleaning the bathroom. Can you help me?
Four. How many eggs are in the fridge?
Sam, how many eggs are there in the fridge?
One, two, three, four, five, six. Six eggs, Mum.
Six. Good. We can make a cake.
Five. What is Sam's favourite drink?
Sam, do you want some milk?
No, thanks. My favourite drink is orange juice.
Orange juice. OK, here you are.
p4: Part Four. Listen and colour. There is one example.
Look at the garden. Can you see the flowers?
Yes. There are lots of flowers.
Colour the flower next to the door. Colour it red.
The flower next to the door. Red. OK!
Can you see the red flower? This is an example. Now you listen and colour.
Now look under the window. Can you see a flower?
Yes. Can I colour it yellow?
Yes. Colour the flower under the window yellow.
There's a flower on the table.
That's right. Colour that flower pink.
Can you see the girl? She's got a flower in her hand.
The flower in the girl's hand. Purple.
Look! There's a flower behind the dog.
Yes. Colour the flower behind the dog blue.
And now the flower next to the tree.
Next to the tree? Can I colour it orange?
